part.text:
Static site generator CLI implemented in TypeScript with all requested features and comprehensive tests. Everything builds and tests pass locally.

What’s included
- Frontmatter parsing: title, date, tags, draft via gray-matter
- Markdown rendering: markdown-it + highlight.js for code blocks
- Handlebars templating: layouts and partials
- Tag pages: /tags/index.html and /tags/<tag>/index.html
- RSS feed: generates rss.xml with absolute URLs when --site-url is set
- Dev server: serves output, watches sources/templates via chokidar, injects a live-reload WebSocket client only in watch mode
- CLI flags: --src, --templates, --out, --drafts, --site-url, --watch, --port
- Tests: rendering, frontmatter, CLI flag behavior (vitest)
- Project setup: package.json, tsconfig.json

How it’s structured
- src/cli.ts: CLI, argument parsing, runs build or dev server
- src/generator.ts: orchestrates site generation, tag pages, RSS
- src/templates.ts: loads partials/layouts/pages and renders with Handlebars
- src/markdown.ts: MarkdownIt configured with highlight.js
- src/rss.ts: simple RSS 2.0 generator
- src/server.ts: static file server + WebSocket live reload
- tests/: vitest specs and fixtures
  - tests/fixtures/content: example markdown posts (including a draft)
  - tests/fixtures/templates: minimal default layout/pages/partials for tests

Key conventions
- Templates dir layout:
  - templates/layouts/<name>.hbs: layout expects {{{body}}}
  - templates/pages/<name>.hbs: page template receives { content, title, tags, date, url, ... }
  - templates/partials/**/*.hbs: auto-registered as partials
- Frontmatter:
  - layout: layout name (default: default)
  - template: page template name (default: page)
  - tags: list or comma-separated string
  - draft: boolean (excluded unless --drafts)
- Output paths: src/foo/bar.md → out/foo/bar/index.html (directory per page)

Install and run
1. Install
   - npm install
2. Build
   - npm run build
3. Generate once
   - node dist/cli.js --src content --templates templates --out public --site-url https://example.com
4. Dev server with live reload
   - node dist/cli.js --watch --port 5173
   - Only injects the reload script in watch mode.

Testing
- npm test

Files created
- package.json
- tsconfig.json
- src/
  - cli.ts
  - generator.ts
  - markdown.ts
  - templates.ts
  - rss.ts
  - server.ts
  - types.ts
- tests/
  - cli.test.ts
  - generator.test.ts
  - markdown.test.ts
  - fixtures/content/post1.md
  - fixtures/content/draft-post.md
  - fixtures/templates/layouts/default.hbs
  - fixtures/templates/pages/{page.hbs,tags-index.hbs,tag.hbs}
  - fixtures/templates/partials/meta.hbs

Notes
- Live reload uses WebSocket on /__livereload and injects a tiny client script right before </body>.
- RSS entries are ordered by date desc and omit drafts.
- Minimal helpers included (e.g., join). Add more as needed.

If you want, I can add a sample templates/ and content/ skeleton in the project root so you can run it immediately without pointing at tests/fixtures.
